authority: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) for Category A projects; State Environment Impact Assessment Authority (SEIAA) for Category B projects

description.en: Environmental Clearance (EC) is a mandatory approval required for setting up new projects or expanding existing ones that may have significant environmental impact. Projects are classified into Category A (appraised at central level by Expert Appraisal Committee) and Category B (appraised at state level by State Expert Appraisal Committee). Category B is further divided into B1 (requiring EIA study and public hearing) and B2 (exempted from EIA study). The process is governed by the EIA Notification 2006 under the Environment (Protection) Act 1986.

verifiedConditions.claim: Environmental Clearance is required only for projects listed in the Schedule to the EIA Notification 2006 (as amended). This includes mining, thermal power, river valley, infrastructure, industries (including petrochemical, cement, metallurgical), and construction projects above specified thresholds.
The project must exceed the threshold limits specified in the Schedule for its sector. Projects below the threshold may not require EC but may need other environmental permits.

unverifiedEligibility: Some states have additional environmental clearance requirements beyond central regulations.
Projects in ecologically sensitive areas (CRZ, Western Ghats, etc.) may need additional clearances.
Expansion projects exceeding specified capacity thresholds also need fresh or amended EC.
Strategic and defence projects may have modified EIA requirements.

requirements.claim: Online application through the Parivesh portal (Single Window for Environment, Forest, Wildlife and CRZ clearances). Form 1 (for projects requiring EIA) or Form 1A (for construction projects and B2 category).
Pre-feasibility report including project description, proposed capacity, site details, land use, water and power requirements, waste generation, and pollution control measures.

Comprehensive Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) report prepared by an accredited EIA consultant, based on Terms of Reference (ToR) approved by the Expert Appraisal Committee. The EIA must cover baseline environmental data, impact prediction, mitigation measures, and an Environmental Management Plan (EMP).

Public hearing conducted by the State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) or Union Territory Pollution Control Committee (UTPCC). The public hearing must be conducted within 45 days of receipt of the request. The EIA report and Executive Summary must be available in the public domain at least 30 days before the hearing.
Land ownership or lease documents, land use certificate, and site location map showing the project boundary and surrounding areas within a 10 km radius.
Consent to Establish (CTE) from the State Pollution Control Board or No Objection Certificate. This may be obtained concurrently with EC for some project categories.

processInformation.claim: Category B projects undergo screening by the State Expert Appraisal Committee (SEAC) to determine whether they require EIA study (B1) or are exempt from EIA (B2). Category A projects proceed directly to scoping.

The Expert Appraisal Committee (EAC) or SEAC prescribes Terms of Reference (ToR) for the EIA study within 60 days of receiving the application. The ToR defines the scope of the environmental studies to be conducted.

EIA study is conducted based on the ToR. After the EIA report is prepared, public consultation (public hearing + written responses) is conducted. The entire EIA including public consultation must be completed within the ToR validity period.

The EAC (for Category A) or SEAC (for Category B) appraises the project based on the application, EIA report (if applicable), public hearing proceedings, and site inspection. The committee makes a recommendation for grant or rejection within 60 days.

The regulatory authority (MoEFCC for Category A, SEIAA for Category B) grants or rejects EC within 45 days of receiving the EAC/SEAC recommendation. The EC is issued with specific conditions that must be complied with during construction and operation.

output.claim: An Environmental Clearance letter is issued containing project details, approved capacity, specific environmental conditions, monitoring requirements, and validity period. EC is typically valid for the project's construction period plus 30 years for operation (for mining, validity equals mine lease period). Half-yearly compliance reports must be submitted to the regulatory authority.

fees.claim: Application fees vary by project category and size. For Category A projects, fees range from Rs. 10,000 to Rs. 50,000 or more. Category B projects may have lower fees set by the respective SEIAA. Additional costs include EIA study (Rs. 5-50 lakhs), public hearing logistics, and consultant fees.

processingTime.applicability: Environmental Clearance from application to decision
processingTime.claim: Category B2 projects (no EIA required) may receive EC within 90 days. Category B1 projects with EIA typically take 120-180 days. Category A projects requiring full EIA and public hearing typically take 180-270 days. Delays may occur due to ToR finalization, EIA study duration, public hearing scheduling, and committee meeting schedules.

sources.title: Parivesh — Single Window for Environment, Forest, Wildlife and CRZ Clearances
sources.publisher: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: Parivesh is the single-window integrated system for online submission and monitoring of proposals for environment, forest, wildlife, and CRZ clearances. All applications for Environmental Clearance must be submitted through this portal.
claimsSupported: All EC applications must be submitted through Parivesh portal.
The portal handles Category A and Category B projects.
Tracking of application status is available online.
Compliance reports are submitted through the portal.
sources.uncertainty: Portal functionality and form requirements may be updated periodically.

sources.title: EIA Notification 2006 (as amended) — Environmental Clearance Procedure
sources.publisher: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The EIA Notification 2006 (S.O. 1533(E), dated 14.09.2006) and subsequent amendments prescribe the procedure for Environmental Clearance including project categorisation, screening, scoping, EIA study, public consultation, and appraisal stages.
claimsSupported: Four-stage process: screening, scoping, public consultation, appraisal.
Category A projects appraised by central EAC; Category B by SEAC.
Category B subdivided into B1 (EIA required) and B2 (EIA exempt).
Statutory timelines for each stage of the EC process.
Public hearing mandatory for Category A and B1 projects.
sources.uncertainty: Multiple amendments have been made since 2006. The 2020 Draft EIA Notification proposed significant changes but faced legal challenges. Current rules may have been further amended.

limitations: This record provides a general overview. Specific requirements vary significantly by project type and sector.
EIA study methodology and scope depend on the Terms of Reference issued for each project.
The record does not cover Forest Clearance, Wildlife Clearance, or CRZ Clearance which may be needed separately.
State-specific SEIAA rules and fee structures are not covered in detail.
Multiple amendments to the EIA Notification make it essential to check the current consolidated version.
The record does not cover post-EC compliance monitoring and reporting in detail.

review.reviewReason: Core EIA framework is verified but frequent amendments to the notification require regular review.
